business_scope.primary_industry_name: Operating and Financial Leasing of Turbofan Aircraft Engines

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1986, as amended by Protocol 2009)
Switzerland–United States Double Taxation Agreement (1996, amended by Protocol 2009)
Switzerland–European Union Free Trade Agreement (1972) via EFTA Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Art. 305bis and 305ter; Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0); Ordinance on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (RFAA, SR 955.01); Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Art. 627a and Art. 697j (UBO register); FINMA Circular 2011/01; Global Forum Act (SR 951.1).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of beneficial owner's passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority / competent civil registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / register of directors and shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home country company registry or statutory agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or professional reference on beneficial owners
Notarized declaration of source of funds and net worth
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in jurisdiction of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for pre-incorporation filings

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on all shareholders, directors, UBOs and authorized signatories against: (i) PEP lists as defined by FATF and Swiss SECO; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) OFAC SDN list; (iv) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; and (v) Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions measures. Screening must be completed before signing and repeated within 5 business days of any UBO change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Central Business Name Index (ZEFIX – Zentraler Firmenindex), operated by Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property; application and formal registration submitted to the competent cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script and may be in one of Switzerland's official languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh). The legal form suffix must appear in the official language of the registered office canton: 'AG' (German), 'SA' (French/Italian in certain cantons), or 'PLC' is not recognized; a foreign-language transliteration must be submitted for any trademark used in non-Latin script. Names must not be false, misleading or infringe existing registered trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is deemed granted upon receipt of valid application by the cantonal commercial register office. If the name is rejected, the applicant or its Swiss attorney must file a written objection (Einsprache/Rekurs) to the competent superior cantonal authority within 10 calendar days. A second-level administrative appeal may be lodged with the competent cantonal administrative court within 30 days. A request for extension of reservation is possible only if no conflicting application was filed in the interim.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is generally not acceptable as the sole registered seat of an Aktiengesellschaft. The registered office must correspond to the actual place of management and have a physical presence (space, personnel or representative, and local business records). A serviced office with a mere mail-forwarding letterbox will fail commercial substance review; a dedicated sub-lease and managed office with in-country physical presence may be accepted only if backed by local personnel and management activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 55% (heightened for aircraft engine leasing due to cross-border asset flow, liquidity and source-of-funds exposure; cantonal tax authorities and financial intermediaries may conduct targeted on-site substance review within the first 12 months of incorporation).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: ZEFIX name search and availability certificate (one company name, one search)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property / Cantonal Commercial Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Ordinance on Commercial Registration Fees (SR 221.411)

Commercial register entry fee (AG, proportional to share capital)
Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate documents (shareholders' and UBO's passport, proof of address, source of funds)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Swiss cantonal chancery / foreign apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Global Hague Apostille Convention charges plus consular fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional legal fees for pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP/OFAC sanctions screening and AML documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of non-official-language documents into the registered office cantonal language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing translation industry rate per certified page

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) of 30 March 1911 (SR 220), as amended; Stock Corporation provisions at Arts. 620-763 OR; incorporation, capital payment and registration at Arts. 629-640 OR; supplementary rules under the Swiss Company Law Reform Act of 19 June 2020 (in force 1 January 2023), and the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the Canton of the registered office, e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug; publication via the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB); federal supervision by the Federal Office of the Register of Commerce (Eidgenössisches Amt für das Handelsregister, EAR) under the Federal Department of Justice and Police.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public notarial deed of incorporation (öffentlich beurkundete Gründungsurkunde) incorporating the Articles of Association (Statuten), together with the Application for Registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) and the Board's Declaration (Erklärung des Verwaltungsrats) confirming that the subscribed capital is paid and freely disposable.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital: CHF 100,000. At least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid in, and in any event no less than CHF 50,000 in aggregate; cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) with a Swiss bank or licensed financial intermediary and released to the company's free disposal only upon entry in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founder subscribes to 100 registered shares, nominal value CHF 1,000 each, constituting the full CHF 100,000 share capital, with CHF 50,000 deposited into a blocked capital account; RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at [address], Switzerland, and the corporate purpose includes the acquisition, operating, and financial leasing of turbofan aircraft engines; RESOLVED, that [Full Name], [Full Name], and [Full Name] are appointed Chair of the Board of Directors, Managing Director, and Secretary, respectively, each with sole signature authority; RESOLVED, that the Board is authorized to execute all Commercial Register filings, open bank accounts, and appoint notaries and advisors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public Office (Notariat) of the Canton of the registered office, e.g., Notariat Kanton Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint a Swiss notary and execute the deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung) recording the Articles of Association, including company name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, share classes and board of directors. The notary authenticates founder signatures and issues a certified notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of each founder
Power of attorney if representatives act on behalf of founders
Background statement for directors, if requested by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises queries, amend the Articles or correct the corporate name and purpose, then re-execute the deed at a supplementary notarial session; no state penalty applies to resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or licensed financial intermediary providing Sperrkonto services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed and incorporation documents to a Swiss financial institution and open a blocked capital deposit account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company in formation. Deposit at least CHF 50,000 of paid-up capital and obtain a written bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) evidencing the deposit and blocking; funds are released only after Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of the authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines onboarding, select an alternative Swiss bank or request the notary to facilitate the blocked account formalities; no penalty applies to re-application with another institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Completion and Execution of the Application Dossier (Anmeldung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and Board of Directors (preparation and signature)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the application for Commercial Register registration, including the Board's declaration that the share capital is fully paid and at the company's free disposal. Sign the declaration in the presence of the notary and consolidate all exhibits for filing.
required_dossiers: Acceptance declarations of board members and auditors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar's preliminary review indicates deficiencies, amend the dossier via supplementary declarations and re-sign the affected forms as instructed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Commercial Register Office and Legal Review (Rechtsprüfung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete formation dossier electronically or in paper with the Commercial Register. The registry performs a legal review of compliance with the Swiss Code of Obligations and the Commercial Register Ordinance; upon approval, the company acquires legal personality as an Aktiengesellschaft.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues deficiency rulings (Verfügungen), respond within the statutory deadline with corrected documents or supplementary declarations; a refusal based on non-remediable legal defects may be appealed to the Cantonal Commission and thereafter to the Federal Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entry in the Commercial Register and SHAB Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office / Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal review is cleared, the Commercial Register enters the company and the entry is published electronically in the SHAB; the company becomes a legal entity on the date of entry. Request a certified extract (Handelsregisterauszug) for banking and counterparty verification.
required_dossiers: No additional filing required; publication is automatic
Certified extract request for bank and supplier proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published entry contains inaccuracies, file a correction request with the registrar, who will issue an amending publication; the cost is borne by the registrar if the error is obvious.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Founding Social Insurance and Municipal Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AHV Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse), Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA), and Municipal Authority (Gemeinde)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the AHV compensation office within 30 days of hiring staff and obtain an employer number; register employees for AHV/IV/EO social insurance and occupational accident insurance with SUVA; complete municipal business and office occupancy registration for the registered premises.
required_dossiers: Office lease agreement and occupancy permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations are cured by immediate filing with the relevant authority and good-faith disclosure; no material penalty applies for an initial late registration if all wage-based contributions are paid with interest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Advisory Notification to the Federal Office of Civil Aviation (Informational)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office of Civil Aviation (FOCA / Bundesamt für Zivilluftfahrt, BAZL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that aircraft engine dry leasing is not an air operation activity and requires no Air Operator Certificate; to the extent the lessor holds asset records for engines installed on Swiss-registered aircraft, coordinate verification of EASA Form 1 or FAA 8130-3 release certificates with FOCA and update the internal asset register accordingly.
required_dossiers: Lease agreements and asset transaction documents
EASA Form 1 or FAA 8130-3 release certificates
Engine technical records and maintenance files, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FOCA queries the asset records, supplement with manufacturer maintenance data and a corrected asset register; engage legal counsel to review lease documentation and certifications.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Office of Civil Aviation (FOCA / Bundesamt für Zivilluftfahrt, BAZL) for aviation asset record oversight; State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for general economic affairs; no industrial licensing board is applicable to commercial aircraft engine dry leasing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – aircraft engine dry leasing neither constitutes air operation (no Air Operator Certificate required) nor industrial manufacturing (no production license); the entity requires only the Commercial Register entry, municipal occupancy permits, and standard employer registrations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category C Registration; pure commercial leasing activity with no manufacturing, combustion, or engine test-cell operations, hence no full environmental impact assessment under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission thresholds apply to the dry-leasing activity; office-sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer ordinances issued under the Federal Water Protection Act (Gewässerschutzgesetz, GSchG), and office waste must be disposed of pursuant to the Federal Ordinance on Waste (VVEA); if the lessor later adds engine storage or light inspection facilities, the VOC Ordinance (VOCV) and cantonal air-hygiene permits would become applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cantonal Fire Insurance Authority (Kantonale Gebäudeversicherung) confirming smoke detectors, extinguishers and escape routes; structural load and office occupancy clearance from the municipal building authority for the registered office; occupational health and safety registration with SUVA under the Swiss Accident Insurance Act (UVG), including the annual premium statement; compliance with the Swiss Labour Act (Arbeitsgesetz, ArG) on office working hours and with the information and consultation rights under the Swiss Code of Obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), portal: www.estv.admin.ch and www.gever.admin.ch (UID registry); cantonal tax authorities (e.g., Cantonal Tax Office of Zug, Finanzdepartement) for direct taxes; Swiss Federal Customs Administration (Oberzolldirektion) for export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) under Swiss Code of Obligations, execute notarial deed, file with Swiss Commercial Register; the Commercial Register automatically assigns the statutory Swiss business identification number (UID / UID-CH, based on Elite ID structure). Step 2: Foreign-controlled AG established in Switzerland must immediately register for VAT with the ESTV on the official VAT registration form (Form 048-S) or through the online 'SAP-MWS' portal, using the UID as VAT number; a Swiss resident AG is liable for VAT irrespective of the CHF 250,000 turnover threshold if it is the registered owner of the enterprise (permanent place of business in Switzerland is not required for registration). Step 3: Obtain employer social insurance registration with the cantonal AHV/AVS compensation office and register for corporate income/capital tax with the competent cantonal tax authority for ordinary assessment; a foreign company with no Swiss place of business but supplying services taxable in Switzerland may use the expedited simplified VAT registration procedure via ESTV.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland applies a unitary entity-level tax model with no US-style Check-the-Box election; no federal tax consolidation exists for direct tax. Available statutory elections relevant to an aircraft engine leasing AG: (i) VAT group taxation election under Art. 57 of the Swiss VAT Act (Mehrwertsteuergesetz), permitting a group of companies to file as a single VAT taxpayer; (ii) participation deduction / capital contribution repayment election to minimise Swiss withholding tax on repatriated funds; (iii) partial taxation procedure for qualifying capital gains; (iv) election under Art. 61 VAT Act to allocate second-hand movable property margins; (v) hybrid mismatch safeguards under Art. 28 VATA granting reduced input VAT recovery where the lessor elects not to treat the foreign lessee as a deemed reseller.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover from January 1, 2025 (previously CHF 100,000); mandatory registration for the SAP/MWS portal with UID; an AG is also strictly liable if it has a permanent establishment, holds a Swiss aviation permit, or issues invoices in Swiss francs for aviation services consumed in Switzerland.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate or government API/Swiss digital stamping regime exists as of the 2025 tax year. Switzerland follows OECD-compliant electronic invoice exchange rules (EN/ISO 20022-Norm, Swiss eBill/QR-bill for payments) but fiscal validation is archiving-based under Art. 70–72 VATA and Art. 21 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; conservative audit trail retention and structured, signed EDI/e-invoice flows are expressly permitted but private. A mandatory nationwide B2B e-invoicing clearance is not enacted; the Federal Council maintains a voluntary period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of aircraft engine dry-leasing services qualifies for 0% VAT (Art. 23 VAT Act) only if the lessor proves that: (i) the recipient is a non-Swiss business (foreign lessee) supplying documentary proof of foreign VAT/UID registration; (ii) the aircraft engine remains located outside Switzerland for the exclusive non-Swiss commercial use; (iii) the leased asset is directly connected to the foreign lessee's aviation operations under ISIC 5223; and (iv) the place-of-supply rule (Art. 7 VATA) places the rental in the foreign country (where recipient has its seat). For goods export, the engine must leave Swiss customs territory physically; zero-rating is denied where tests are rebutted by customs or tax audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (e-dec / NCTS or AVN summary declaration) evidencing the physical departure of the turbine engine from Swiss fiscal territory
Original or certified Copy of the Air Waybill (AWB) or Bill of Lading naming the foreign lessee as ultimate consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or equivalent bank settlement proof for lease rentals received from the foreign lessee
Lease agreement (dry-lease contract) stating operator, registration marks, engine serial number, and delivery/redelivery airports
Foreign lessee's VAT/company registration certificate (e.g., EU VAT ID, FAA/ICAO evidence) and engine logbook or maintenance movement card indicating non-Swiss location during the lease term
Power of Attorney (PoA) and UID certificate of the Swiss AG for export control verification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV and federal customs conduct exporter audits of aviation lessors under Arts. 77–79 VATA; missing export proof triggers retroactive VAT assessment at 8.1% on the full leasing revenue, plus compound statutory interest (4% per annum) from the invoice date. Under Art. 96 VATA, cases of contained tax evasion attract a fine of up to 4x the evaded tax; intentional, concealed fraud under Art. 97 VATA triggers a fine of up to 8x the evaded amount and up to 3 years imprisonment for responsible officers, with confiscation; the limitation period for clawback is 10 years (Art. 42 f. VAT Act). Customs sanctions under Art. 116–117 Customs Act and Swiss Criminal Code Art. 146 also apply concurrently. The 180-day statutory FX repatriation deadline stated above is the contractual safe harbour under Swiss transfer-pricing practice (2025 OECD alignments); repatriation beyond 180 days shifts the burden of proof onto the taxpayer for commercial necessity and triggers a deemed distribution risk under withholding tax with possible 35% WHT liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque Nationale Suisse) acting under the National Bank Act (SR 951.11), with FINMA supervising banks and SECO enforcing Swiss sanctions and export-control measures. The SNB has no exchange-control mandate; its foreign-exchange operations serve only monetary policy, including discretionary market intervention to counter excessive CHF appreciation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Switzerland maintains a completely liberalized capital and current account regime with no general exchange-control law and no SNB approval requirement for cross-border capital movements. Capital account: a foreign parent or investor may subscribe shares or grant a shareholder loan to CH_AG without authorization; the non-resident real-property restriction of the Lex Koller is inapplicable to aircraft-engine leasing. Current account: lease rentals, MRO payments, and insurance settlements in any convertible currency flow freely. The only material profit-remittance hurdle is fiscal: outbound dividends from a Swiss AG are subject to 35% anticipatory Swiss withholding tax at distribution, reducible or refundable to 0% under an applicable double-tax treaty (typically 0% for shareholders holding 10% or more; 15% or 5% for portfolio investors) via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) relief or refund procedure. No exchange-control permit, capital-export declaration, or SNB registration is required for such remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Switzerland imposes neither statutory surrender nor mandatory conversion of export proceeds. CH_AG may receive USD/EUR lease rental income from foreign lessees and retain it in non-CHF accounts onshore or offshore without any timing or conversion-ratio constraint. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations, collected by banks under SNB reporting rules for aggregate cross-border flows, apply; these carry no convertibility or repatriation requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (CHF) plus multi-currency Operational Treasury Account (CHF/USD/EUR sub-ledgers) with dedicated Aviation & Asset Finance desk for security-deposit custody, escrow services, and SWIFT clearing.
Operational Current Account (CHF) with USD/EUR clearing sub-accounts and escrow depositary services for lessee security deposits; state-guaranteed institution with conservative AMLA onboarding.
Operational Account (CHF/EUR) with SEPA and SWIFT cross-border clearing capability; adequate for medium-sized operational flows and treasury settlements.
Domestic CHF Operational Account suitable for payroll, supplier payments and tax disbursements; limited aviation asset-leasing product depth and escrow capabilities.
Digital multi-currency Operating Account (CHF/USD/EUR) with online FX execution; acceptable as a secondary clearing rail but deficient in escrow, LC, and documentary credit products.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury solution; Medium only as an ancillary bill-pay rail. A foreign EMI (e.g., UK/Lithuanian/Dutch-licensed electronic money institutions or banking-as-a-service providers) is not FINMA-licensed under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act (FinIA, SR 954.1), has no direct access to Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC/euroSIC), cannot issue Swiss IBANs (CHxx), and cannot provide capital-escrow, commercial LC, standby LC, or documentary-custody services expected by an aircraft-engine lessor. Use of such EMIs should be strictly limited to low-value outbound disbursements and API-driven virtual sub-accounts swept daily into a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank account; all cash concentration, lease-rent receipt, security-deposit escrow, and large-value SWIFT traffic must be executed through a licensed Swiss banking institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss law (FINMA Circular 2016/07, as amended) permits identification by video or electronic means for natural persons, but remote-only onboarding is generally unsuccessful for an enhanced-risk aviation-leasing entity. At least one director or authorized signatory must attend an in-person KYC interview at the Swiss bank's branch (UBS/ZKB standard practice), presenting original passport, residence proof, and the certified board resolution appointing the signatory. Foreign UBOs may be verified through a video interview combined with notarized and apostilled identity documents, or through a delegated KYC certificate issued by an AMLA-regulated Swiss fiduciary under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA, SR 955.0). Pure online account opening without any human interview is refused by major Swiss banks for companies in the aircraft-engine leasing sector.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain routed through a trust, private foundation, or LLC in a low-tax or bank-secrecy jurisdiction without demonstrated source of wealth, combined with a medium-risk asset-leasing business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO table covering every legal entity holding more than 10% of CH_AG; source-of-wealth report with audited financial statements, disposal agreements, or credit agreements; apostilled passport copies of all identified UBOs; bank reference letter for the UBO from a top-200 global bank; and CH_AG economic-substance evidence including a Zurich registered office lease, local director appointment, current Commercial Register excerpt, board minutes, and a corporate payroll record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or negative-news screening triggers: lessee, payment corridor, or engine end-user touching SECO, FINMA, or US OFAC sanctions lists (e.g., Russian carriers, Iran Air, Syrian Arab Airlines) or export-control red flags on engine transfer eligibility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions compliance program referencing the Swiss Embargo Act (SR 946.203) and FINMA Circulars; executed dry-lease agreement containing an express anti-sanctions warranty, absolute sublease prohibition, and blocking clause; end-user certificate and dual-use/export-control classification dossier for the specific engine model; independent flight-tracker data demonstrating engine deployment outside prohibited airspace; negative World-Check and Dow Jones screening snapshots for all contracting parties, actual operators, and UBOs; and a Swiss legal opinion confirming no SECO/OFAC nexus for reviewed transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Federal Direct Tax and Cantonal/Communal Corporate Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (e.g., Zürich/Genève Canton tax office) and Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for direct federal tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal-year end (financial year ending 31 December: due 30 June; cantonal extension routinely granted to 30 September)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing default assessment, statutory late interest at 5% p.a. on tax due, and administrative penalty (max. CHF 10,000); wilful evasion may attract criminal fine or custodial sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (if annual VAT settlement scheme)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year VAT period: 60 days after year-end (28 February/1 March); quarterly filers follow quarter deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% p.a. and penalty up to 100% of the tax evaded; repeated failure may trigger administrative enforcement and criminal complaint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Board-audited annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) including balance sheet, income statement, annex and management report; approval by the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the AGM; copy filed together with the tax return to the cantonal tax authority; not publicly filed with the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months from closing date (31 December year-end: no later than 30 June before AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ignoring the obligation leads to director civil liability and, after formal notice, court order to present accounts; in persistent breach, cantonal authority may apply for liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited or ordinary auditor's report dated and approved in advance of the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's shareholders and board of directors (retained in minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the annual general meeting and within six months of year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Without valid audit report when audit is compulsory, the AGM cannot validly approve the annual accounts; the commercial-register office may refuse registration of amendments until report is remedied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the current share capital structure and beneficial ownership transparency (Transparenzregister) as part of the tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration / Transparency Register (Beneficial Ownership Register) maintained according to the revised Anti-Money Laundering Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing notification duty: within 10 days after any share transfer; no free-standing annual 'renewal' filing in current Swiss law
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with transparency register and reporting duties: penalty orders up to CHF 500,000 for legal persons; additional per-person fines for responsible officers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (independent) audit required for AG where, in two consecutive fiscal years, two or three thresholds are exceeded: assets > CHF 20m, turnover > CHF 40m, >250 average full-time employees; mandatory also for listed, regulated or 500+ shareholder entities. Otherwise limited audit applies; limited audit may be waived upon unanimous AGM resolution only when the company has 10 or fewer full-time staff and no one shareholder holds more than 10% (Art. 727, 727a CO).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957a ff. CO) as mandatory accounting law; applied as Swiss GAAP FER for true-and-fair presentation; IFRS permitted for reportable listed entities or if required by a competent authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law contains no annual UBO confirmation form. However, the board of directors is under a continuous duty to record and file any changes of beneficial owners to the Transparency Register within 10 days; the statutory annual tax-declaration asks for confirmation of the company's capital structure, and the company secretary must produce an updated register of members before every general meeting. On any substantial transfer of the aircraft-engine leasing shares, notarization and commercial-register notification is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienbuch / registre des actions)
Restricted audit report file and annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – 2,500 per year for domiciliation, corporate secretariat and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 10,000 for a standard limited audit of an aircraft-engine leasing AG with a mid-size balance sheet; ordinary extended audit quotes may exceed USD 25,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 4.4% Swiss federal direct tax on profit (Art. 68 DBG) plus cantonal and communal profit taxes; aggregate headline rate 11.9%-21.0% depending on canton of formal seat (e.g., Zug approx. 11.9%, Zurich approx. 19.7%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Post-TRAF 2020 reliefs: participation exemption (100% relief on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income), patent box (up to 90% income relief for qualifying IP), R&D super-deduction (up to 150% of qualifying expenditure in most cantons), notional interest deduction (selected cantons only), 7-year loss carryforward (no carryback), step-up/fair-market-value relief on transition, and flexible Swiss depreciation practices for aviation assets (declining-balance or asset-pool amortisation of engine portfolios).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal/federal corporate income tax return for Aktiengesellschaften, designated 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' (form designation varies by canton); filed electronically through the tax e-portal of the canton of registered seat (e.g., eTax ZH in Zurich, zPortal in Zug, é-démarches in Geneva); the Federal Direct Tax assessment is made on the basis of the same combined return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. No quarterly corporate income tax return is required; cantonal provisional profit-tax instalments may be collected quarterly or semi-annually, but the legal entity files only once after the accounting year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Federal statutory minimum: the return must be filed within 30 days of service of the request (Art. 124 DBG). In ordinary cantonal practice for a 31 December balance-sheet date the deadline is set around 30 June of the following year, with extensions of 2-3 months granted on written request; foreign-parent groups typically receive extended filing windows if consolidated reporting is not ready.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The AG's fiscal year, balance-sheet date and commercial register identification; the annual accounts must close to a 12-month period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent must align the Swiss AG's reporting period with the aviation leasing cycle; an off-calendar year is accepted if properly disclosed and consistently used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit/loss before tax as per the statutory profit-and-loss statement (Art. 959b CO), including engine lease income, maintenance reserves and impairment charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this line; the Swiss AG remains fully tax-resident and reports its worldwide income, with no look-through to the foreign parent's consolidated results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs of non-deductible expenses and hidden profit elements: disproportional financing costs, non-business reserves, direct/indirect profit distributions, excessive interest or fees paid to shareholders and related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent must substantiate all cross-border lease payments, engine purchase prices and financing charges; undocumented amounts are recharacterised as hidden profit distributions subject to 35% withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: loss carryforward (maximum 7 years), participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (Art. 69 DBG), patent box deduction (Art. 24a/69a DBG), R&D deduction, and arm's-length depreciation on aircraft engines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Participation relief requires proof of the qualifying holding (at least 10% of share capital or CHF 1 million market value) through the Swiss AG's share register; the foreign parent's TRC is referenced but does not create a Swiss deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit of the AG after all adjustments; this is the assessment base for federal and cantonal profit tax and forms the basis for dividend distribution capacity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount is not allocable to a Swiss permanent establishment of the foreign parent; it belongs to the Swiss AG as a distinct taxable person and is the baseline for future dividend WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of shareholder loans, receivables, guarantees, debt waivers and interest charged on non-resident balances; Swiss thin-capitalisation practice applies an acceptable debt-to-equity ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors must attach loan agreements and arm's-length interest computations; excessive debt is reclassified as equity and the interest deduction is denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer-pricing disclosure and supporting documentation for the aircraft-engine dry-leasing business: method used (TNMM, CUP, cost plus, profit split) and substance indicators; CbC notification via the Swiss AEOI portal when consolidated group revenue is at least CHF 900 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent must supply its tax residence certificate and group organisational chart when treaty relief is invoked; an advance ruling from the cantonal/FTA tax authorities should be referenced.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers default interest on the assessed tax (currently 4.5% per annum) and an administrative fine of up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 174/175 DBG; after a penal deadline the tax authority issues an estimated assessment, reversing the burden of proof; intentional concealment constitutes tax evasion punishable by a fine of 1x-3x of the evaded federal tax, with the same scaling under cantonal law; directors who knowingly sign false returns are personally prosecutable under Art. 175/181 DBG.
